source_text: Has tamen elocutionum diversitates, quas tu non solum non imitaris, verum etiam criminaris, quarum nos adiuvamur officiis, non linguarum omnium, sed graecae et latinae cultus invenit. Ceterum linguae aliae, quae naturales vocantur, ob hoc quod nihil eis aut opum aut nitoris studia secuta contulerint, simplicibus omnino nominibus membrorum abutuntur; unde et apud Hebraeos, quorum sermone Scripturarum puritas continetur, propriis omnia vocabulis indicantur.
pass_a_gloss: These diversities of expressions nevertheless, which you not only do not imitate but even accuse, by whose offices we are helped, the culture not of all tongues but of Greek and Latin found. For the rest, other tongues, which are called natural, on account of this that studies of wealth or of polish have conferred nothing on them, altogether misuse simple names of members; whence also among the Hebrews, by whose speech the purity of the Scriptures is held, all things are indicated by proper words.

lemmas.lexica: LS naturalis; Blaise malum naturale=evil as a nature
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself

pass_b_english: The varieties of expression whose service I use, and which you not only fail to imitate but even attack, were developed by refinement in Greek and Latin, not in every language. Other languages are called natural because subsequent cultivation has brought them neither richness nor polish; they use entirely simple names for bodily parts. Thus among the Hebrews, in whose language Scripture’s purity is contained, everything is indicated by its own proper word.

choices.why: Julian's Manichaean charge: an evil that is a nature, not a will's act.
Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
Julian's sacred writings; keep Scripture, not 'Bible' as a later book-name.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
